title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1969-02-27
lineage: SBD 16-Track Master Reel > Rough Mix DAT > DATx3 > Digital Sound Card > WAV > SHN > WAV > Cool Edit > CDWAV > SHN

ai_review.summary: An excellent soundboard capture of one of ’69’s most electrifying shows, highlighted by a cosmic Dark Star, soaring St. Stephen and blistering Eleven/Lovelight.
ai_review.review: The recording is a clean, open‑sounding soundboard tape with a slightly forward drum mix that lets every nuance shine. Musically the performance is pure fire – Mountains of the Moon segues into a legendary Dark Star, followed by an incendiary St Stephen/William Tell and the thunderous Eleven/Lovelight pair, plus the wild Cryptical > O‑1 > Cryptical suite and a monster Doin’ That Rag jam. Energy is consistently high and the band is locked in, making this a benchmark 1969 concert.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 enthusiastic reviews (virtually all 5‑star) praise both the musical performance and the audio quality; only minor non‑musical complaints appear, so the combined show + recording rating is near top‑tier.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, open mix with good instrument separation; Bobby’s drums are a touch louder than on Live/Dead but add excitement. No noticeable drop‑outs or muddiness.

standout_songs: Mountains of the Moon → Dark Star transition
Cryptical Envelopment > O‑1 > Cryptical (Other One suite)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Seamless transitions – Mountains of the Moon sets up Dark Star, which leads into a powerful St. Stephen/William Tell; the second set builds with The Eleven and Lovelight before the sprawling Other One suite, keeping momentum high throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His solo on Dark Star is described as soaring, jazzy, and ‘cosmic’; co‑leads with the organ are praised.
band_member_comments.Phil: Called a “thunder” on bass during The Eleven; his playing is highlighted as a key driver of the show’s intensity.
band_member_comments.Bob: Noted for fluid right‑hand rhythmic fills and strong vocal contributions, especially on Doin' That Rag.
band_member_comments.Keys: Organ interplay with Jerry is called stellar (especially on The Other One suite).
band_member_comments.Drums: Bobby (the drummer) is louder in the mix than on Live/Dead; his introductions and “Thumpy & Drumstick” banter are celebrated.
